title: Closer than anyone, and on your side in every dark
subtitle: Al-Waliyy: the Protecting Friend who stays near the believers and leads them to light
intro: Al-Waliyy (الْوَلِيُّ) means the Protecting Friend: the One who is close to the believers, loves them, takes care of their affairs, supports them and brings them out of darkness into light. It means that whoever turns to Allah is never without a friend who is near, loyal and able to help in every situation.

root.sense: Wala' is nearness, one thing directly following or touching another. Arabs used it for a saddle resting right against a horse's back. From closeness came care and responsibility: a guardian is the one closest to a child's affairs. Al-Waliyy is near to His servants and takes charge of them.

row.title: Nearness
sub: close as a saddle to the back

row.title: Care
sub: He takes charge of your affairs

row.title: Out into light
sub: in this world and the next

row.title: My safety rests on people and tools
sub: the police, the doctor, the contacts

knowing: Al-Waliyy carries two things at once: closeness and care. Think of a lifeguard at a pool. It is his job to watch everyone, keep the rules and pull out anyone who is drowning. He is responsible for them. Al-Waliyy is like that, but He never takes a break, never looks away and never fails. {idea}He is near to the believers and has taken their affairs into His hands.{/idea}

This name is different from Al-Wali, the Governor, who manages the affairs of all creation. Al-Waliyy describes a special friendship: love, support and protection for those who believe. Allah is the Waliyy of those who believe; He brings them out of darknesses into the light (2:257). He is the ally of the righteous (7:196, 45:19).

In the Quran this name often comes with An-Nasir, the Helper. A guardian is responsible for you by right; a helper is anyone who steps in when you are cornered. {idea}Allah is both: enough as Protector and enough as Helper (4:45).{/idea}
seeing: Yusuf was betrayed by his brothers, sold for a few coins, falsely accused and imprisoned. At the end, with his family restored, he turned to Allah and said: You are my Protecting Friend in this world and the Hereafter (12:101). Looking back, he saw that the well, the prison and the palace had all been under the care of Al-Waliyy. {reward}Sometimes the protection was the very place he would never have chosen.{/reward}

Allah describes His friendship with a picture: those who believe He brings from darkness into light, while those who take false protectors are led from light into darkness (2:257). Imagine a room in a blackout, everyone lost, and one person with a light who leads them to the door. That is what Al-Waliyy does for a heart lost in sin, doubt or despair.
It is He who sends down rain after people had lost hope and spreads His mercy, and He is Al-Waliyy, Al-Hamid (42:28). His friendship often arrives exactly when hope has run out.
trusting: We easily rely on the means as if they were the protectors: the police, the ambulance, the medicine, the boss. These are blessings and we use them. But {trap}taking the tools as your protectors{/trap} leaves you helpless when they fail. To Allah belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth. Every means is one of His soldiers, sent or withheld by Him.

Al-Waliyy also guards you from false friends. Shaytan promises that if you drop prayer, fasting or honesty you will get ahead. That is taking him as a protector, and he will abandon you. Allah promises forgiveness and bounty (2:268). Whose friendship will you trust?

And when you feel far from Him, remember the hadith qudsi in Sahih al-Bukhari: Allah says His servant draws near to Him through the obligations, then keeps drawing nearer through voluntary deeds until He loves him, and then if he asks, He gives him, and if he seeks refuge, He protects him. {reward}The door to His friendship is open, one step at a time.{/reward}
loving: Everyone wants one friend who will never betray them, never get tired of them, and always show up. {idea}Al-Waliyy is that friend, and He invites you to be His.{/idea}
The more you live with Him as your Protector, the more you realise how often He has rescued you, and love for Him becomes the most natural thing in the world.
now: Your closest friend has stopped answering your messages, and the group chat has gone quiet when you join. You feel suddenly very alone in the city. {idea}Al-Waliyy has not gone anywhere; He is nearer than any friend has ever been.{/idea} Open the Quran tonight and spend ten minutes with the Friend who never leaves.
old: When people let me down, I am left with no one on my side.
new: Al-Waliyy is my Protecting Friend, so I always have Someone near who takes care of me.
try: Add one small voluntary deed today, two extra rak'ahs or a quiet charity, as a step toward Al-Waliyy.

dua.text: Ya Waliyy, You are my Protector in this world and the next. Take me out of every darkness into Your light, and never leave me in the care of anyone but You.
dua.note: Call on Him by this name when you feel abandoned or lost; Yusuf prayed You are my Protector in this world and the Hereafter after a life of trials (12:101).

pairs.why: Al-Waliyy Al-Hamid (42:28): He protects and rescues His friends, and He is praised for every rescue, even the ones they did not notice.
Because He is your close Friend, handing your affairs to Him as Al-Wakil becomes natural and easy.
Al-Waliyy is near and takes your side; Al-Hafiz keeps you safe and preserves your faith from harm.

faq.a: Al-Waliyy means the Protecting Friend. Allah is close to the believers, loves them, supports them, takes charge of their affairs and brings them out of darkness into light (2:257). It describes a special care for those who believe and do good.

faq.q: What is the difference between Al-Waliyy and Al-Wali?
faq.a: Al-Waliyy is the Protecting Friend, describing Allah's special closeness, love and support for the believers. Al-Wali is the Governor, the One who manages and administers the affairs of all creation. Both come from the same root meaning nearness and taking charge, but they highlight different sides.

faq.q: What is a wali of Allah?
faq.a: A wali of Allah is a believer who draws close to Him through faith and righteous deeds. According to a hadith qudsi in Sahih al-Bukhari, a servant draws near through the obligations, then through voluntary acts, until Allah loves him and answers and protects him.
